RATIONALE The College of Pharmacy presently consists of three Departments: The Department of Applied Pharmaceutical Science (APS); The Department of Biomedical Science (BMS) and the Department of Pharmacy Practice (PHP).
Faculty in PHP are primarily clinicians, who are directly involved in patient care and as a result are primarily based at clinical sites throughout the state.
In contrast, faculty in APS and BMS are based at the Kingston campus.
Furthermore, with the exception of the Pharmacoepidemiology and Pharmacoeconomics (PE/PE) Section of APS, the research activities of APS and BMS are primarily laboratory based.
As pharmaceutical science and biomedical science has evolved in the last decade there has been an increasing overlap in the research activities of the two departments.
However, the present departmental structure discourages collaboration and hinders interaction between and among faculty.

The proposed departmental structure would address this problem and hopefully lead to cross-fertilization of research efforts between the two existing departments.
Owing to the more practice oriented research activities of the PE/PE section of APS, a more logical placement for this section would be within the department of PHP.
These organizational changes will also enable the College to address its graduate program and consider ways to make the program more cost-effective and to better prepare the graduates for careers in pharmaceutical and biological science.
The new structure would have minimal effect on the courses offered in College of Pharmacy.
The College of Pharmacy's main teaching responsibility is delivery of the Doctor of Pharmacy curriculum.
Since this is a College-wide integrated curriculum, the proposed restructuring would only lead to some recoding and renumbering of courses.

3 B.RATIONALE This organizational change is being proposed because the Physical Therapy Program can better fulfill its mission to educate competent doctors of physical therapy who can provide skilled patient care in a variety of settings, conduct clinical research, and provide service to the community at large if it is an academic department within the College of Human Science and Services rather than a program within the Kinesiology Department.
The mission of the Physical Therapy Program focuses on professional, graduate rather than undergraduate education as is the case in the Kinesiology Department.
There are no common students between the two units nor does faculty teach across the units.
The reorganization will allow PT faculty to focus their efforts on continued development and advancement of the program, clinical and basic science research related to the profession and provision of service to the community and profession.
The Physical Therapy Program has functioned autonomously within the (Department of Physical Education now renamed) Kinesiology Department since its inception in 1991.

It has had its own faculty, support staff, facilities, and budget from the very beginning as a requirement of professional accreditation.
Further, due to accreditation requirements, the Program Director has maintained direct communication with the Dean of the College and was a regular participant at College Management meetings.
A self-study report for the Commission on Accreditation in Physical Therapy Education was recently completed in preparation for a site visit that occurred in September 2005.
It was during this self- evaluation that the faculty recognized that the Program was intended to be a separate entity within the college from its development and that separation would allow for better overall functioning of the program.
With the recent move from the masters of physical therapy to the doctor of physical therapy, the program is even more out of place being located within the Kinesiology Department.
Separation will allow better collaboration between the Physical Therapy Program and other departments such as Communicative Disorders and Biology.

This re- organization will simplify day-to-day operations and clarify evaluation of program activities because data will no longer be combined with that of the Kinesiology department.
Please note that no new resources are needed to affect this organizational change.
C.INSTITUTIONAL ROLE This organizational change is consistent with the published role and mission of URI.
The Department of Physical Therapy will have all of the responsibilities of a Department.
In addition, it will provide added value to the University through its recognition as the only Physical Therapy Program in the state and via the clinic, which provides physical therapy to citizens of Rhode Island.

4 D.INTERINSTITUTIONAL CONSIDERATIONS The projected impact of this organizational change on the other public higher educational institutions in Rhode Island is nil. Other institutions in Rhode Island will not be affected by this change because the Physical Therapy Program is not a new program and is not competing with other programs in the state for students or resources. There are no cooperative arrangements with other institutions relative to this organizational change. E.EVALUATION The Physical Therapy Program is fully accredited through the Commission on Accreditation in Physical Therapy Education (CAPTE). Evaluation of the program is on going and includes both direct and indirect measures of clearly defined outcomes. Examples of outcome measures include the percentage of students who pass the National Physical Therapy Licensure Exam, the percentage of students who receive outstanding grades on the clinical performance instrument, a tool that is used nationally to evaluate the performance of students in the clinical setting, and responses from employers gathered both on surveys and in focus groups. Effective this semester, the PT program will begin using the electronic portfolio system recently purchased by URI called “True Outcomes”. Data from these evaluations will be used to make necessary changes in the doctor of physical therapy degree program.
